title: Water War: India, Pakistan and the Indus
oneLine: India has suspended the treaty that shares the Indus rivers; Pakistan calls diversion an act of war. In this scenario, a massacre near Jammu lights the fuse again.

whoIsWho.stance: Promised that 'blood and water cannot flow together'; under pressure to answer any attack.
Pakistan's field marshal and real power; facing India in the east and the Taliban in the west.
Pakistan's prime minister, governing alongside the army.
The 1960 water deal India holds 'in abeyance' since April 2025.

whyItMatters: Two nuclear-armed states, and a river system that feeds most of Pakistan's farms. In May 2025 they fought a four-day drone and missile war; the next round could move faster and further.

timeline.text: Partition: India and Pakistan both claim Kashmir.
The World Bank brokers the Indus Waters Treaty.
Gunmen kill 26 people at Pahalgam in Kashmir.
India puts the Indus Waters Treaty 'in abeyance'.
Operation Sindoor: four days of strikes, then a ceasefire.
A constitutional amendment makes Munir Chief of Defence Forces.
Pakistan declares 'open war' on the Afghan Taliban.
